articles.title: With the main opposition party suspended, Ecuador returns to the polls
articles.author: BreakThrough News
articles.content_excerpt: On November 12, the campaigns for Ecuador’s local elections formally began. This Sunday, November 29, voters will elect prefects, mayors, city council members, and members of local boards. Historically, local elections have reflected the level of support or opposition to the current government. In this sense, right-wing president Daniel Noboa has more at stake than just a simple popular election. This is especially true when considering the last elections (which centered on four referendum questions) held on November 16, 2025. In those elections, Noboa suffered a fourfold electoral defeat, as the majority of Ecuadorians rejected his attempt to repeal the current constitution – which guarantees rights – in favor of a neoliberal one. articles.title: Morocco jails four Sahrawi students over political prisoner protest
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: Condemning the sentencing of four Sahrawi students for taking part in a peaceful demonstration in solidarity with Sahrawi political prisoners, human rights groups in Western Sahara have called for greater international scrutiny of Morocco as an occupying power. The four jailed students are Brahim Babit, Salah Eddine Sbar, El Hussein Chihab, and Mohamed Lemrabet, studying at Zohr University in the Moroccan city of Agadir. On October 12, they traveled over 500 km north to the national capital, Rabat, to attend the demonstration. articles.title: One million students across Europe strike against war and rearmament
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: More than 50 student organizations in 27 European countries launched an international strike against war and militarization on Friday, November 20, drawing a million of young people onto the streets. Students issued joint demands including an end to rearmament and all forms of conscription, investment in education and social services, and solidarity with oppressed peoples around the world. They also declared resistance to growing authoritarian trends in the region. “We are protesting to claim our right to a better future, and we are aware that if we stand united, no one will be able to stop us from taking it,” said Alessandro Di Miceli from the Italian organization Rete della Conoscenza. articles.title: Ansar Allah advances towards Saudi stronghold Aden
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: As the renewed fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Ansar Allah-led Yemeni Armed Forces enters its fourth month, developments on the ground indicate that the conflict has reached a critical threshold. However, what Riyadh and its allies could not achieve over the past decade in Yemen seems far from attainable at this point, as Ansar Allah continues to expand its territorial control and target vital Saudi sites. The last week saw a remarkable advance by Ansar Allah towards Aden, the seat of the Yemeni interim government, backed by Saudi Arabia and Western countries.
